title: How India Turned Smartphone Imports Into a 165x Global Megafactory

scenes.ttsText: Ten years ago, three out of every four smartphones in India were imported.
scenes.displayMarkup: Ten years ago, three out of every four *smartphones* in India were *imported.*

scenes.ttsText: Today, ninety-nine point two percent of phones sold in India are made right here. How? Stay with me, because one number in this video explains everything.
scenes.displayMarkup: Today, *99.2%* of phones sold in India are *made right here.* Stay with me — *one number* explains *everything.*

scenes.ttsText: Go back to twenty fourteen. India exported just one thousand five hundred and sixty-six crore rupees of mobile phones. Barely a footnote in global trade.
scenes.displayMarkup: In *2014,* India exported just *₹1,566 crore* of mobile phones — ranked a tiny *#153* in our exports.

scenes.ttsText: And today? Two lakh sixty thousand crore rupees! That is one hundred and sixty-five times more — now India's number one tech export!
scenes.displayMarkup: And *today?* *₹2,60,000 crore!* That's *165 times* more — now India's *#1 tech export!*

scenes.ttsText: So how did that happen? India stopped just importing boxes and switched on P L I in mission mode. Mobile factories jumped from just two to over three hundred!
scenes.displayMarkup: India switched on *PLI* in *mission mode.* Mobile factories jumped from just *2* to over *300!*

scenes.ttsText: And this isn't basic screwdriver work anymore. Precision enclosures, camera modules, and multilayer circuit boards — engineered across Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Uttar Pradesh.
scenes.displayMarkup: No ordinary assembly: precision *enclosures,* optics, and *circuit boards* built across *India.*

scenes.ttsText: Remember that locked number? Today, India builds more than ten smartphones every single second — including one in every seven iPhones on Earth!
scenes.displayMarkup: Every. Single. *Second:* *10+ phones* built — including *1 in every 7* iPhones on *Earth!*

scenes.ttsText: And the world is buying. Millions of Made-in-India phones now ship to the United States, the U K, the Netherlands, the U A E, and Japan.
scenes.displayMarkup: Millions of *Made-in-India* phones now ship to the *US,* *UK,* *Europe,* *UAE,* and *Japan.*

scenes.ttsText: Now, the honest part. We still import most of the tiny nanometer silicon chips inside those phones. That's the real catch.
scenes.displayMarkup: Now the *honest* part: we still import most of the tiny *silicon chips* inside.

scenes.ttsText: Which is why five semiconductor fabs worth one point five two lakh crore are rising in Gujarat and Assam. Because a country that only assembles phones is a factory. A country that builds the chips is a superpower.
scenes.displayMarkup: A country that only assembles is a *factory.* A country that builds the *chips* is a *superpower.*

scenes.ttsText: Look at the phone in your hand right now — iPhone, Samsung, or OnePlus? Drop one word in the comments.
